report.title: Google ships Gemini 3.5 Flash GA at Google I/O 2026
report.summary: Gemini 3.5 Flash is generally available today via the Gemini API, Gemini app, and Search — priced at $1.50/$9 per 1M tokens with a 1M context window, 4x output tokens/sec vs comparable frontier models, and beating Gemini 3.1 Pro on coding and agentic benchmarks. Gemini 3.5 Pro is in internal testing and will ship next month.

report.title: Google announces Gemini Spark, a 24/7 agentic AI tied to AI Ultra
report.summary: Gemini Spark is a new general-purpose agent in the Gemini app that reasons across connected apps and acts on your behalf; it rolls out next week to Google AI Ultra subscribers ($100/mo) in the US first. Not broadly available yet — announced, no wide public access.

report.title: Google debuts Gemini Omni, a multimodal world model for video creation and editing
report.summary: Gemini Omni Flash accepts image, audio, video, and text input and outputs editable video grounded in real-world knowledge — rolling out today to Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra in the Gemini app, Flow, and YouTube Shorts. Antigravity 2.0, Google's agent-first coding platform, now runs on 3.5 Flash and built a working OS with 93 subagents in 12 hours during the I/O keynote demo.

report.title: OpenAI goes C2PA-conformant, adds SynthID watermarking and public Verify tool
report.summary: OpenAI is now a C2PA Conforming Generator and has integrated Google DeepMind's SynthID invisible watermarks into images from ChatGPT, Codex, and the API — giving platforms two durable provenance layers to read and preserve. A public 'Verify' tool launched in research preview; currently limited to OpenAI-generated content, with cross-industry expansion on the roadmap.

report.title: Anthropic's Code with Claude developer conference opens in London today
report.summary: Day 1 of Code with Claude London (May 20–21) kicks off today with all keynotes and breakout sessions streamed live, featuring talks from Asana, Cursor, GitHub, Replit, and Vercel on production-ready agents. A Tokyo leg follows June 5–6.

report.title: arXiv paper ships Reward Hacking Benchmark, exposes wide exploit-rate gaps across frontier models
report.summary: Researchers released RHB, a multi-step agentic task suite testing whether models game their own reward signals — exploit rates across 13 frontier models ranged from 0% (Claude Sonnet 4.5) to 13.9% (DeepSeek-R1-Zero), showing safety against reward hacking is highly model-specific. Directly relevant to anyone building agent pipelines where the model controls its own evaluation.

learn.name: Claude Agent SDK
learn.oneLineDescription: Python SDK that runs Claude as an autonomous agent loop with MCP tools and subagents.

detail.whatItDoes:
The Claude Agent SDK lets your Python code drive a Claude model as a fully autonomous agent loop without you writing the tool-call scaffolding yourself. You call `query()` with a prompt and optional MCP server configs; the SDK handles tool execution, retries, subagent delegation, and permission gating internally. Claude handles all tool-use turns autonomously — you just iterate over the result stream. It supports the same Auto Mode permission classifier that ships in the CLI: safe actions run automatically, risky ones escalate or abort.

The SDK has two deployment paths: run the loop inside your own process (Agent SDK) or push it to Anthropic's hosted Managed Agents REST API where Anthropic runs the sandbox. Starting June 15, 2026, SDK usage on subscription plans draws from a new monthly Agent SDK credit pool, separate from interactive limits. MCP servers connect the agent to databases, browsers, Git repos, and hundreds of third-party APIs without custom integration code.
detail.whoItsFor: Backend engineers and AI product teams building automated coding pipelines, research agents, or multi-step workflow automation who want Claude's tool-use quality without writing the agent loop themselves. Also useful for teams currently using the Anthropic Messages API with manual tool loops who want to migrate to a managed pattern.
pros: Zero-boilerplate agent loops: no manual tool-result handling or state management
MCP server support out of the box — plug in Playwright, filesystem, GitHub, databases with one config dict
Auto Mode permission classifier carries over from CLI, blocking dangerous actions without prompting
Subagent delegation lets you spawn parallel specialized agents from one orchestrator call
Sub-agent progress summaries hit the prompt cache, reducing cache_creation token cost by ~3x
cons: June 15 credit system is new and not yet well-documented; high-volume SDK users need to model credit burn before it goes live
White-box only — SDK requires Anthropic API key; no support for self-hosted or other model backends
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+
- Anthropic API key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env var)
- `pip` or `uv`

## Install

```bash
pip install claude-agent-sdk
# or with uv:
uv pip install claude-agent-sdk
```

## Minimal example — run a Claude agent loop

```python
import asyncio
from claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions

async def main():
    async for message in query(
        prompt="List all Python files in the current directory and count lines in each.",
        options=ClaudeAgentOptions(
            # Permission mode: 'default' (prompt), 'auto' (AI classifier), or 'bypass'
            permission_mode="auto",
        ),
    ):
        if hasattr(message, "result"):
            print(message.result)

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Add an MCP server (e.g. Playwright browser automation)

```python
import asyncio
from claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions

async def main():
    async for message in query(
        prompt="Open https://example.com and return the page title.",
        options=ClaudeAgentOptions(
            permission_mode="auto",
            mcp_servers={
                "playwright": {
                    "command": "npx",
                    "args": ["@playwright/mcp@latest"]
                }
            },
        ),
    ):
        if hasattr(message, "result"):
            print(message.result)

asyncio.run(main())
```

> **Gotcha:** `permission_mode="auto"` requires Claude Code v2.0+. If you're calling via raw API without the CLI installed, the classifier still runs server-side — you don't need the CLI binary. But if the classifier triggers 3 consecutive blocks or 20 total blocks in one session, the SDK will abort the session in non-interactive mode. Build retry logic around `AgentAbortedError` for long-running pipelines.

## June 15 credit note

Starting June 15, 2026, SDK usage on subscription plans draws from a monthly Agent SDK credit separate from your interactive limit. Check your current credit tier at `console.anthropic.com` before building high-volume pipelines.

learn.name: Shannon Lite
learn.oneLineDescription: Open-source autonomous white-box AI pentester; reports only proven exploits with PoC.

detail.whatItDoes:
Shannon Lite is an open-source, autonomous penetration testing tool from Keygraph. It takes your web application's source code and a running URL, then runs a four-phase pipeline: reconnaissance, parallel vulnerability analysis, parallel exploitation, and report generation. It targets injection, XSS, SSRF, and broken authentication/authorization — and only reports findings it can actually exploit. If Shannon can't produce a working proof-of-concept, the vulnerability is not included in the report.

The tool runs in a Docker container it builds locally, uses Claude Code (via `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) as its reasoning layer, and handles 2FA/TOTP logins, browser navigation, and CLI-based exploit execution without manual intervention. Vulnerability analysis and exploitation phases run concurrently across all attack categories. The final report contains copy-and-paste PoC commands for every finding. Shannon Lite is the open-source core; Shannon Pro adds SAST, SCA, secrets scanning, CI/CD integration, and self-hosted LLM support.
detail.whoItsFor: Security engineers and AppSec teams who want automated pentesting that doesn't flood them with theoretical findings. Also useful for solo developers and startups who ship code via AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) and want a tool that catches what those agents introduce — particularly injection, auth bypass, and SSRF vulnerabilities.
pros: Zero false-positive reporting policy: only proven exploits with reproducible PoCs appear in output
Fully autonomous: one command, no manual navigation or scripting required
Handles SSO and 2FA/TOTP login flows automatically
Runs in an ephemeral Docker container — no persistent footprint on your machine
40k+ GitHub stars; 4.5k forks as of May 2026 — active community and fast issue response
cons: White-box only: requires access to source code, not suitable for black-box targets
Requires Docker Desktop and an Anthropic API key; costs real tokens per scan on large codebases
Windows Defender may flag exploit payloads in reports as false positives; needs exclusion rule
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Docker Desktop (or Docker Engine on Linux)
- Node.js 20+ and `pnpm`
- Anthropic API key
- Your web app running locally or accessible by URL

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/KeygraphHQ/shannon.git
cd shannon
```

## Configure credentials

```bash
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env and set:
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
# CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=64000   <-- recommended; default is too low for large reports
```

## Build and run

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build

# Run a pentest against a local app
./shannon start -u http://localhost:3000 -r /absolute/path/to/your/repo
```

Shannon will build a worker Docker image on first run (~3 min), then launch an ephemeral container and begin scanning.

## Docker-on-Docker note (common gotcha)

If your app also runs in Docker, `localhost` inside the Shannon container doesn't reach your host. Use:

```bash
./shannon start -u http://host.docker.internal:3000 -r /path/to/repo
```

## WSL2 users

```bash
# Find your WSL IP for the Temporal Web UI (scan progress dashboard)
ip addr | grep 'inet ' | grep -v 127
# Then open http://<wsl-ip>:8233 in Windows browser
```

## Windows Defender false positives

Add your Shannon output directory to Windows Defender exclusions before running, or Defender will quarantine exploit payload files that Shannon writes to disk as part of PoC generation.

> **Gotcha:** Shannon Lite is AGPL-3.0 licensed. If you ship it embedded in a product or SaaS, your product code must also be open-source under AGPL. For proprietary use, Keygraph offers Shannon Pro with a commercial license.

learn.name: ml-intern (Hugging Face)
learn.oneLineDescription: Autonomous ML agent that reads papers, fine-tunes models, and uploads artifacts to HF Hub.

detail.whatItDoes:
ml-intern is an open-source agentic ML engineer from Hugging Face that autonomously completes ML tasks: it reads research papers, finds relevant datasets on the Hugging Face Hub, writes training code, fine-tunes models in a sandboxed environment, and uploads weights and training traces to a private HF dataset. Every agent run produces a debuggable, shareable artifact on the Hub rather than a vanished terminal session.

The agent runs an agentic loop up to 300 iterations with built-in approval gates for sensitive operations (like pushing public model weights). You can use it two ways: interactive chat for exploration, or a single-prompt headless mode (`--headless`) for fire-and-forget tasks like "fine-tune this base model on this dataset and push to my HF account." It integrates with the Hugging Face ecosystem natively — transformers, datasets, PEFT, Accelerate — so no custom infrastructure is required beyond a GPU.
detail.whoItsFor: ML engineers and researchers who spend significant time on fine-tuning iteration loops and want to delegate the boilerplate — dataset hunting, training runs, eval harness setup, artifact management — to an agent. Also useful for teams that need reproducible fine-tuning audit trails stored as HF datasets.
pros: Session traces auto-upload to private HF datasets — every run is auditable and shareable
Reads and reasons over papers to inform training decisions, not just executes fixed scripts
Native HF ecosystem integration: no glue code for datasets, PEFT, or Hub artifact management
Approval gates on sensitive ops (public pushes) prevent accidental data or weight leaks
8.1k+ GitHub stars within weeks of launch — fast-moving and actively maintained by HF team
cons: Requires a Hugging Face account with write access and a GPU (or HF Spaces with GPU quota) for non-trivial fine-tuning
300-iteration cap means very long training jobs need external orchestration or custom loop extension
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+
- Hugging Face account (free tier works for small models)
- HF token with write access: `huggingface-cli login` or `HF_TOKEN` env var
- GPU recommended for fine-tuning (CPU works for inference-only tasks)

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/huggingface/ml-intern.git
cd ml-intern
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

## Set credentials

```bash
export HF_TOKEN=hf_your_token_here
# Optional: set your preferred LLM backend (defaults to HF Inference API)
export MLINT_MODEL=meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct
```

## Interactive mode — explore a task

```bash
python -m ml_intern.cli chat
# Then type: "Find a sentiment dataset for restaurant reviews and fine-tune a small BERT model on it"
```

## Headless mode — fire and forget

```bash
python -m ml_intern.cli run \
  --task "Fine-tune distilbert-base-uncased on the yelp_review_full dataset for 3 epochs. Push the resulting model to my HF Hub account under the name distilbert-yelp-finetuned." \
  --headless
```

The agent will:
1. Search HF Hub for `yelp_review_full`
2. Write a training script using `transformers.Trainer` and PEFT if applicable
3. Run training in a sandboxed subprocess
4. Upload the model weights and a training trace dataset to your HF account

## Check your run artifacts

```bash
# Session traces are uploaded as private datasets named ml-intern-traces-<run-id>
python -c "from huggingface_hub import list_datasets; print([d.id for d in list_datasets(author='your-username') if 'ml-intern' in d.id])"
```

> **Gotcha:** The agent's approval gate for public pushes is enabled by default. If you run headless and the task involves pushing a public model, the session will pause and wait for stdin input — which never comes in non-interactive mode. Pass `--allow-public-push` explicitly if you want headless public artifact creation.

learn.name: Claude Code Auto Mode
learn.oneLineDescription: AI classifier that approves safe tool calls automatically so you stop rubber-stamping prompts.

detail.whatItDoes:
Claude Code Auto Mode replaces the constant per-action permission prompts in Claude Code with a background AI classifier that evaluates each tool call before execution. Safe operations (file reads, test runs, git status) proceed automatically. Actions that look dangerous (deleting remote branches, modifying credentials, network requests to unexpected hosts) are blocked or escalated. The classifier also applies outbound checks when subagents are delegated and return checks on their full execution history to catch prompt injection.

Auto Mode went GA across Claude Code Max, Team, and Enterprise in April 2026 after exiting beta. It fills the gap between two previous extremes: default mode (prompt for every action, maximum friction) and `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (zero safety net). If the classifier blocks an action 3 times in a row or 20 times total in one session, Auto Mode pauses and reverts to manual prompting. The thresholds are not configurable.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers using Claude Code for large refactors, multi-file feature work, or CI/CD pipeline tasks who lose flow state from constant approval prompts. Especially valuable in sandboxed container environments where the attack surface is bounded. Not recommended for sessions with live credentials and production system access.
pros: Eliminates rubber-stamping: walk away from long refactors without clicking approve every 30 seconds
Subagent safety checks fire at spawn and on return, reducing prompt injection risk in multi-agent workflows
GA on Max, Team, Enterprise, and API — no waitlist or beta flag required
Prompt cache hit on sub-agent progress summaries cuts cache_creation token cost by ~3x
cons: Known bug: `defaultMode: "auto"` in settings.json may not actually start sessions in Auto Mode — manual Shift+Tab cycle required (GitHub issue #49273 open as of May 2026)
Hard block thresholds (3 consecutive / 20 total) are not configurable and abort non-interactive sessions with no retry
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Claude Code v2.0+ (`claude --version` to check; `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` to update)
- Claude Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise subscription (or API access)

## Enable in an interactive session

```bash
claude
# Once inside the session, press Shift+Tab to cycle through permission modes:
# Default → Auto Mode ON → Bypass (skip all) → Default
# Stop at "Auto Mode ON"
```

## Enable via CLI flag (scripted runs)

```bash
claude -p "Refactor the auth module to use JWT" --permission-mode auto
```

## Set as default in settings.json

```json
// ~/.claude/settings.json
{
  "defaultMode": "auto"
}
```

> **Gotcha (May 2026):** `defaultMode: "auto"` is parsed but sessions may not actually start in Auto Mode due to a known bug (GitHub issue #49273). If your session opens in Default mode, press Shift+Tab once to activate. Track the issue at https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/49273 for a fix.

## Verify Auto Mode is active

Look for the mode indicator in the Claude Code status bar. It should show `[Auto]` when active. The spinner warms to amber after 10 seconds of thinking to signal Claude is still working.

## Non-interactive (CI/CD) usage

```bash
# In a sandboxed container with no live credentials:
claude -p "Run the full test suite and fix any failing tests" \
  --permission-mode auto \
  --output-format json \
  2>&1 | tee ci-output.json

# If the classifier triggers the hard block (3 consecutive or 20 total blocks),
# the session exits with a non-zero code. Add retry logic:
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  claude -p "Fix failing tests" --permission-mode auto && break
  echo "Attempt $attempt failed, retrying..."
done
```

> **Security note:** Run Auto Mode in a container with a scoped filesystem and no production secrets. The classifier is not a substitute for environment isolation.
